instruction: We act for Pakairt Outdoor Apparel, Inc., the licensee under its software license arrangement with Sairan Systems, LLC. Pakairt wants a clear view of where it stands before it relies on the deal. Please review all ten documents in the folder and send me a memo. For each issue, give the document and section where it appears, explain why it matters for Pakairt, and recommend a fix.

rubric.text: The response concludes that each automatic renewal under the License Agreement runs for 60 months (five years), with only a 30-day non-renewal window, rather than the 12-month renewals in the term sheet. It identifies the issue as arising in License Agreement Section 12.2 or SOW Section 4.1, explains why this matters to Pakairt, and recommends a fix.

The response concludes that Pakairt's May 4, 2026 notice electing not to proceed with Phase 2 was sent after the Side Letter's 45-day window had closed (the window ran from the March 2, 2026 Phase 1 Acceptance Date), so the election is likely ineffective. It identifies the issue as arising in Side Letter Section 2 or the May 4, 2026 notice letter, explains why this matters to Pakairt, and recommends a fix.
hints: 45 days after the Phase 1 Acceptance Date

rubric.text: The response concludes that Pakairt's one-way indemnity to Sairan under the DPA is not subject to the liability cap (it is uncapped). It identifies the issue as arising in License Agreement Section 10.3 or DPA Section 9, explains why this matters to Pakairt, and recommends a fix.

The response concludes that Pakairt's exclusivity obligation extends beyond PLM to functions such as retail point-of-sale and e-commerce merchandising, exceeding the PLM-only exclusivity in the term sheet. It identifies the issue as arising in License Agreement Section 2.5 or SOW Section 1.2, explains why this matters to Pakairt, and recommends a fix.
hints: term sheet limited exclusivity to PLM

rubric.text: The response concludes that Sairan may assign the agreement to any person, including a Pakairt competitor, without Pakairt's consent. It identifies the issue as arising in License Agreement Section 15.3, explains why this matters to Pakairt, and recommends a fix.
hints: assign to any person without Licensee's consent

rubric.text: The response states that the annual license fee is $1,140,000.
The response is presented as a memo, such as one addressed to the supervising partner or bearing memo headings.
The response organises its analysis issue by issue, giving each issue its own location, significance and recommended fix.
The response claims that Pakairt's May 4, 2026 Phase 2 opt-out notice was timely under the Side Letter.
The response claims that Pakairt's DPA indemnity is limited by the 12-month-fees liability cap.
